Model equations

pdmS7 documentation

Source: vignettes/model-equations.Rmd
model-equations.Rmd

This page is the reference: every equation pdmS7 implements, with Moore (2007) equation numbers for the PDM; the snow model follows equations 2.1 to 2.8 of the Institute of Hydrology PACK report. Notes mark where the implementation interprets or corrects the source. For what the equations mean, start with How the PDM works and How the snow model works.

Units and symbols

All depths are millimetres averaged over the catchment; time is in hours internally.

Symbol Meaning Unit
pp, ee, dd, vv Rain, actual evaporation, recharge and runoff depths per interval mm
ss Catchment-average soil water mm
cc A local store’s capacity mm
CC Common filling level of the stores mm
F(c)F(c) Fraction of the catchment with capacity no greater than cc fraction
XX, uu, qq Routing storage, inflow rate and outflow rate mm; mm/h; mm/h
Δt\Delta t Model interval h
AA Catchment area km²

Rain and potential evaporation are interval totals, not rates. q_m3s is the mean flow over the interval; q_end_m3s is the flow at its end.

PDM

Soil moisture: the capacity distribution (Eq. 2-3, 7, 9, 18-20)

For a filling level CC, the fraction of the catchment that is saturated is F(C)F(C), and the mean water stored across the catchment is

s(C)=∫0C[1−F(c)]dc,smax=E[c].s(C)=\int_0^C [1-F(c)]\,dc, \qquad s_{\max}=E[c].

capacity_cdf() returns F(C)F(C); storage_from_capacity() evaluates s(C)s(C) and capacity_from_storage() inverts it; capacity_mean() returns smaxs_{\max}, the mean capacity, which is not the largest local capacity.

With a=cmina=c_{\min}, z=cmaxz=c_{\max} and w=z−aw=z-a, the five capacity families are:

Family (type) CDF inside its support Mean capacity
Pareto (pareto) 1−[(z−c)/w]b1-[(z-c)/w]^b a+w/(b+1)a+w/(b+1)
Rectangular (rectangular) (c−a)/w(c-a)/w (a+z)/2(a+z)/2
Symmetric triangular (triangular) 2(c−a)2/w22(c-a)^2/w^2 below the midpoint; 1−2(z−c)2/w21-2(z-c)^2/w^2 above (a+z)/2(a+z)/2
Exponential (exponential) 1−exp(−c/μ)1-\exp(-c/\mu) for c≥0c\ge 0 μ\mu
Lognormal (lognormal) Φ((logc−μL)/σL)\Phi((\log c-\mu_L)/\sigma_L) for c>0c>0 exp(μL+σL2/2)\exp(\mu_L+\sigma_L^2/2)

Φ\Phi is the standard normal CDF. CDFs are zero below and one above a bounded support. Pareto with b=0b=0 is a point mass at cmaxc_{\max}. The printed Appendix A formulas for the rectangular and triangular families assume cmin=0c_{\min}=0; pdmS7 uses the general forms above. The triangular and lognormal storage functions are inverted exactly (cubic solution, and Newton iteration from a bracket); see source-notes.md.

Evaporation, recharge and runoff (Eq. 5-8, 10, 15-17)

Rain is first multiplied by the rainfall factor: p=fcpinputp=f_c\,p_{\mathrm{input}}. With soil storage ss at the start of the interval and potential evaporation epe_p:

ereq=ep[1−(1−ssmax)be].(Eq. 8)e_{\mathrm{req}}=e_p\left[1-\left(1-\frac{s}{s_{\max}}\right)^{b_e}\right].\qquad\text{(Eq. 8)}

Evaporation is allocated first and recharge second, so neither can overdraw the store:

e=min(ereq,s+p),d=min(dreq,max(0,s+p−e)).e=\min(e_{\mathrm{req}},\,s+p),\qquad d=\min(d_{\mathrm{req}},\,\max(0,\,s+p-e)).

The net depth n=p−e−dn=p-e-d fills the stores. When n>0n>0,

C=s−1(sold),snew=s(C+n),v=n−(snew−sold).(Eq. 15-17)C=s^{-1}(s_{\mathrm{old}}),\quad s_{\mathrm{new}}=s(C+n),\quad v=n-(s_{\mathrm{new}}-s_{\mathrm{old}}).\qquad\text{(Eq. 15-17)}

Whatever cannot be stored becomes direct runoff vv. When n≤0n\le 0 storage falls and runoff is zero.

Recharge (Eq. 10-13)

Standard recharge drains soil water above a threshold sts_t:

dreq=max(0,s−st)bgkgΔt.(Eq. 10)d_{\mathrm{req}}=\frac{\max(0,\,s-s_t)^{b_g}}{k_g}\,\Delta t.\qquad\text{(Eq. 10)}

kgk_g has units h·mmbg−1^{b_g-1}, which are hours only when bg=1b_g=1.

Demand recharge depends on the groundwater deficit. With XmaxX_{\max} the groundwater storage giving outflow qsatq_{\mathrm{sat}}, g=min(1,max(0,(Xmax−X)/Xmax))g=\min(1,\max(0,(X_{\max}-X)/X_{\max})) and dsat=qsatΔtd_{\mathrm{sat}}=q_{\mathrm{sat}}\Delta t:

dreq=[dsat+(smax−dsat)min(1,(g/α)β)]ssmax.(Eq. 11-13)d_{\mathrm{req}}=\left[d_{\mathrm{sat}}+(s_{\max}-d_{\mathrm{sat}}) \min\left(1,(g/\alpha)^\beta\right)\right]\frac{s}{s_{\max}}.\qquad\text{(Eq. 11-13)}

This is written as a depth per interval, so it depends on the time step, and it needs qsatΔt≤smaxq_{\mathrm{sat}}\Delta t\le s_{\max} and a single groundwater store.

Split recharge has no soil drainage: direct runoff is divided, αv\alpha v to the surface store and (1−α)v(1-\alpha)v to groundwater.

Routing (Eq. 21-27)

Each routing store obeys

dXdt=u−q(X).(Eq. 21-23)\frac{dX}{dt}=u-q(X).\qquad\text{(Eq. 21-23)}

Option Outflow law Notes
Linear q=X/kbq=X/k_b Exact solution
Quadratic q=X2/kbq=X^2/k_b Exact solution
Cubic q=X3/kbq=X^3/k_b Adaptive integration; optional Smith recurrence (Eq. 24-25)
Power q=kXmq=kX^m Adaptive integration (Eq. 21-23)
Cascade Ẋ1=u−X1/k1\dot X_1=u-X_1/k_1, Ẋ2=X1/k1−X2/k2\dot X_2=X_1/k_1-X_2/k_2 Exact two-store solution (Eq. 26-27)
Exponential q=exp(γ+aX)q=\exp(\gamma+aX) XX is a signed log-storage coordinate, not a tank

Inflow is constant within an interval. The Smith recurrence is accurate only for steps up to about an hour; see Choosing model components.

Delay and discharge

After an outlet delay tdt_d (fractional delays split water between neighbouring intervals), the mean flow is

Qmean=A3.6Vfast+VslowΔt+qc,Q_{\mathrm{mean}}=\frac{A}{3.6}\,\frac{V_{\mathrm{fast}}+V_{\mathrm{slow}}}{\Delta t}+q_c,

where VV are the routed depths in mm over the interval and qcq_c is a constant external adjustment in m³/s that does not draw on the model’s stores.

Water balance

ϵ=old storage+p−e−natural outflow−new storage,\epsilon=\text{old storage}+p-e-\text{natural outflow}-\text{new storage},

with storage including the soil, routing stores and water in the delay queue. pdmS7 reports ϵ\epsilon for every step; it is zero to rounding.

Forecast updating (Eq. 28-42)

State correction (Eq. 28-30) distributes the flow error at the forecast origin between the surface and groundwater stores, with gains, in proportional, super-proportional or non-proportional form; ARMA error prediction (Eq. 31-42) forecasts the error series in additive or log form, with pdmS7’s ar equal to −ϕ-\phi in Moore’s notation. See Forecast updating.

PACK snow model

Rain or snow

With corrected precipitation pp, temperature TT and snow threshold TsT_s:

psnow={p,T<Ts0,T≥Ts,prain=p−psnow.p_{\mathrm{snow}}=\begin{cases}p,&T<T_s\\0,&T\ge T_s\end{cases},\qquad p_{\mathrm{rain}}=p-p_{\mathrm{snow}}.

New snow enters the dry store WW and restores full cover.

Melt

With snow-covered fraction FF, melt factor ff, melt threshold TmT_m and internal step hh:

m=min(W+psnow,Ffmax(0,T−Tm)h),Wnew=W+psnow−m.m=\min\left(W+p_{\mathrm{snow}},\;F f\max(0,T-T_m)\,h\right),\qquad W_{\mathrm{new}}=W+p_{\mathrm{snow}}-m.

Liquid water and drainage

Rain on covered ground and meltwater enter the wet store SS:

S′=S+Fprain+m,Sc=r(S′+Wnew).S'=S+F p_{\mathrm{rain}}+m,\qquad S_c=r\,(S'+W_{\mathrm{new}}).

D={0,T<Tcmin{S′,h[k1S′+k2max(S′−Sc,0)]},T≥TcD=\begin{cases}0,&T<T_c\\ \min\{S',\;h[k_1S'+k_2\max(S'-S_c,0)]\},&T\ge T_c\end{cases}

Snew=S′−D,peffective=D+(1−F)prain.S_{\mathrm{new}}=S'-D,\qquad p_{\mathrm{effective}}=D+(1-F)\,p_{\mathrm{rain}}.

Cold weather stops drainage but does not refreeze liquid water.

Snow cover (PACK Figure 2.2)

With total water content θ=W+S\theta=W+S and θc\theta_c the content for complete cover:

F0(θ)=min(1,log(1+θ)log(1+θc)).F_0(\theta)=\min\left(1,\frac{\log(1+\theta)}{\log(1+\theta_c)}\right).

After fresh snow, cover returns to F0F_0 along a path anchored at the previous content θa\theta_a and cover FaF_a, over the final fraction α\alpha of the fresh-snow excursion NN:

F(θ)=max[F0(θ),Fa+(1−Fa)min(1,θ−θaαN)]for θ>θa.F(\theta)=\max\left[F_0(\theta),\;F_a+(1-F_a)\min\left(1,\frac{\theta-\theta_a}{\alpha N}\right)\right] \quad\text{for }\theta>\theta_a.

The report gives prose and a diagram rather than full event logic; pdmS7’s reading is recorded in source-notes.md.

Internal steps and balance

Each interval is divided into

Nsub=⌈max(60Δtmax_step_min,Δt(k1+k2),1)⌉N_{\mathrm{sub}}=\left\lceil\max\left(\frac{60\,\Delta t}{\text{max\_step\_min}},\; \Delta t\,(k_1+k_2),\;1\right)\right\rceil

steps to keep the drainage calculation stable. The snow balance residual is

ϵsnow=(W+S)old+pcorrected−peffective−(W+S)new.\epsilon_{\mathrm{snow}}=(W+S)_{\mathrm{old}}+p_{\mathrm{corrected}} -p_{\mathrm{effective}}-(W+S)_{\mathrm{new}}.

When PACK feeds the PDM, the PDM’s fcf_c still multiplies the effective rain; set it to 1 to avoid correcting precipitation twice.
